headerNote: vermont.gov / firesafety.vermont.gov — see final sections). **CORRECTED July 10, 2026: Vermont DOES credential chimney sweeps — see §1a. CORRECTED Sep 15, 2026: the T4 certificate is a Fire & Building Safety Code requirement that reaches "public buildings" (including rentals) but NOT owner-occupied single-family homes (§1a); Vermont has no statewide IRC — the current code is the 2025 VFBSC on the 2021 IBC/NFPA 1/NFPA 101 (§5); the sweep rule now also accepts NCSG (§1a).**

verification.heading: Verification pass — September 25, 2026
verification.markdown:
Checked 2026-09-25 by verification agent (sweep #2). Laws cited as of Sep 2026. **Method note:** WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted). Job 1 was done by primary-host fetch, not search, using four kinds of source:
- the 2025–2026 Acts & Resolves index (legislature.vermont.gov/bill/acts/2026 — all 179 acts listed, read in a browser because the table is script-rendered);
- bill-status pages;
- the history lines of every cited section;
- the DFS codes page and the OPR residential-contractor page.

- **T4 scope vs owner-occupied single-family (coordinator item):** CONFIRMED, still a two-text inference.
  - The Fire & Building Safety Code's § 1 (Title, Intent and Authority) ends with item (d): "These rules apply to 'public buildings' as defined by 20 V.S.A Chapter 173." No item (e) or all-building exception follows.
  - § 1:1.13 opens: "A certificate of fitness is required for all individuals performing activities related to fire or life safety based on the qualifications as follows". That sentence sits inside rules scoped to public buildings.
  - 20 V.S.A. § 2730(b)(1) excludes "An owner-occupied single-family residence, unless used for a purpose described in subsection (a)". § 2730(b)(4) excludes an owner-occupied single-family home with an ADU "unless rented overnight or for a longer term". The § 2730 history shows no 2025–26 amendment.
  - 20 V.S.A. § 2731 (amended 2025 No. 69, § 24, eff. July 1, 2025, adding an energy-education module for gas/oil trades only) sets the T4 fee at $30 but states no building-type scope. The DFS T4 page states no scope either.
  - Result: not required for an owner-occupied single-family home by any text read; required for work in public buildings including rentals.
  - Sources: https://firesafety.vermont.gov/sites/firesafety/files/Rules/VFBSC%202025%20Rules%20Final.pdf ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/20/173/02730 ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/20/173/02731 ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/fullchapter/20/173 ; https://firesafety.vermont.gov/licensing/t4-chimney-sweep. Evidence class GOV/DOC.
- **Licensing threshold, 26 V.S.A. § 5501:** RE-CONFIRMED. The section requires registration "prior to contracting with a homeowner to perform residential construction in exchange for consideration of more than $10,000.00". § 5509 sets insurance at $1M/$2M. § 5502(2)(A) exempts DPS-certified trades. All §§ 5501–5510 history lines show "Added 2021, No. 182 (Adj. Sess.), § 14, eff. July 1, 2022" with no later amendment. Sources: https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/26/106/05501 ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/fullchapter/26/106. Evidence class GOV.
- **H.718:** RESOLVED (closed). The official title is "An act relating to building energy efficiency". Last action was 3/27/2026 (Senate first reading, referred to Natural Resources and Energy), and the page shows "No act information found". It was not enacted, so the $10,000 threshold stands. Source: https://legislature.vermont.gov/bill/status/2026/H.718. Evidence class GOV.
- **Seller disclosure:** RE-CONFIRMED as no general statutory form. The only statutory seller disclosure found is flood-related (27 V.S.A. § 380), amended 2025 No. 52, § 2, eff. Sept 1, 2025. That section now covers the FIRM map, flood history during ownership, and flood-insurance status; §3 is updated. The SPIR remains voluntary: Peet Law says "Vermont does not legally require sellers to complete a SPIR" (REF). Sources: https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/27/005/00380 (GOV) ; https://floodready.vermont.gov/disclosure (GOV) ; peetlaw.com (REF).
- **CO law, 9 V.S.A. §§ 2881–2883:** RE-CONFIRMED, with a 2025 amendment noted. 2025 No. 69, § 23 (eff. July 1, 2025) amended all three sections. The current text requires "photoelectric-type or UL 217 compliant" smoke alarms plus CO alarms. It requires the seller to certify at closing ("signed and dated by the seller"), and keeps the buyer's 10-day certified-mail notice with a 10-day seller cure. No title defect results. §6 is updated. Sources: https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/09/077/02881 ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/09/077/02882 ; https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/09/077/02883. Evidence class GOV.
- **3-day cancel, 9 V.S.A. § 2454:** RE-CONFIRMED. The consumer may cancel "until midnight of the third business day after the day on which the consumer has signed an agreement". The last amendment was 1974. Source: https://legislature.vermont.gov/statutes/section/09/063/02454. Evidence class GOV.
- **Code cycle:** RE-CONFIRMED. The 2025 VFBSC has been effective since 11/05/25 (NFPA 1/101 2021, IBC 2021, NFPA 70 2023, IPC 2024). A precision fix: the rules adopt the 2021 IEBC for "structural requirements only". The DFS codes page shows no 2026 rulemaking notice. Source: https://firesafety.vermont.gov/buildingcode/codes. Evidence class GOV.
- **2026 law-change sweep:** done by primary-host fetch, not search. The 179 acts of the 2025–26 biennium were filtered for contractor, building, fire, chimney, wood, CO/smoke, disclosure, consumer, OPR, housing and energy terms. Relevant finds:

sections.title: State licensing and registration
sections.markdown: **Vermont credentials chimney sweeping for work in public buildings — see §1a.** For *contracting*, there is only a thin registration. Vermont historically licensed no general/residential contractors; **Act 182 (2021 Adj. Sess., eff. Jul 1, 2022), codified at 26 V.S.A. chapter 106**, created a **Residential Contractor Registration** administered by the Secretary of State's Office of Professional Regulation (OPR). Under **26 V.S.A. § 5501(a)** a person must **register with OPR before contracting with a homeowner to perform residential construction for more than $10,000**; **§ 5509** requires **$1,000,000 per-occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate liability insurance** and a written contract for work over $10,000 (STATE LAW). **Registration is a registry entry + insurance/disclosure attestation — there is NO exam and no competence test**; chimney sweeping and small repairs of $10,000 or less fall outside it. Public registry: **sos.vermont.gov/residential-contractors**. Regulators told VTDigger in Apr 2026 that few contractors are registered and a bill (H.718, which VTDigger says would create a contractor-registry task force) was under discussion; **H.718 was not enacted** (bill-status page, Sep 25, 2026: last action 3/27/2026, referred to Senate Natural Resources and Energy; "No act information found"), and **no enacted change to chapter 106 was found** (every §§ 5501–5510 history line reads only "Added 2021, No. 182 (Adj. Sess.), § 14, eff. July 1, 2022"; the 2025–26 OPR omnibus acts, Nos. 58 and 119, do not touch chapter 106 per their official act summaries). OPR's page notes registration has been required since April 1, 2023.

sections.rawHeading: 1a · Sweep Certificate of Fitness (GOV — high confidence; scope resolved Sep 15, 2026)
sections.title: Sweep Certificate of Fitness
sections.markdown:
**The Division of Fire Safety (Dept. of Public Safety) issues a T4 Chimney Sweep Certificate of Fitness (TQP)** for those who "clean, maintain and evaluate chimneys and solid fuel burning appliances" (firesafety.vermont.gov/licensing/t4-chimney-sweep). The rule text is **2025 Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code § 1:1.13.1(5)**: "Sweeping, maintenance and evaluation of Chimneys and Solid Fuel Burning Appliances – A current certificate from the Chimney Safety Institute of America, Certified Chimney Professionals, OR National Chimney Sweep Guild (NCSG) at the Certified Chimney Professional Level. Eight hours of related instruction is required for certificate renewal every three years." (The DFS web page still lists only CSIA or CCP; the rule adds NCSG.) TQP certifications run three years; the statutory certificate fee is **$30** (20 V.S.A. § 2731(c)(4)(J): "Chimney and solid fuel burning appliance cleaning, maintenance, and evaluation: $30.00"). **Public roster: data.vermont.gov "T4 Certifications" (data.vermont.gov/Government/T4-Certifications/tjh9-m65b).** DFS also issues Gas Certificates of Fitness.

**Scope — who actually has to hold it (RESOLVED from rule + statute text):** the Code states "These rules apply to 'public buildings' as defined by 20 V.S.A. Chapter 173." **20 V.S.A. § 2730** defines public buildings to include rental accommodations, workplaces, offices, hotels, restaurants and similar, and **excludes "an owner-occupied single-family residence, unless used for a purpose described in subsection (a)"** (an owner-occupied home with an ADU is excluded unless the ADU is rented). So **the T4 requirement governs sweep work in public buildings — rentals, multi-family, commercial — and does not legally require a certificate to sweep an owner-occupied single-family home.** A related rule, **§ 1:11.5.1.7.1**, requires fuel-fired heating appliances in covered buildings to be inspected at least once every 2 years by persons certified under § 1.13 — so landlords, not homeowners, carry a recurring certified-inspection duty. *(This scope reading combines the Code's applicability clause with § 2730; DFS has not published a sentence stating it for T4 specifically. Page copy should say "required for work in rentals and other public buildings; not required by state rule for an owner-occupied single-family home — though many sweeps who hold it work in both.")*

Interlock: **26 V.S.A. § 5502(2)(A)** exempts from OPR registration "a tradesperson licensed, registered, or certified by the Department of Public Safety acting within the scope of his or her license, registration, or certification" (and § 5502(2)(B) businesses working primarily through such people) — a certified sweep may lawfully be absent from the SOS registry, so check the DFS roster first.

sections.title: What the credential does not test
sections.markdown: Narrower than in most states, but not closed. The OPR registry verifies **insurance and identity, not competence**, and jobs of $10,000 or less need no registration. The **T4 certificate writes NCSG-CCP/CCP/CSIA certification into a state credential — but only for work in public buildings.** For an owner-occupied single-family home, the state requires no sweep credential at all, and no Vermont credential tests masonry *repair* competence. An independent audit still adds the layers the state doesn't check for homeowners (cert check, insurance below $10k, photo evidence, review integrity).

sections.rawHeading: 3 · Home sale (REF/GOV — SPIR customary, not statutory)
sections.title: Seller disclosure when a home sells
sections.markdown: Vermont sellers owe a common-law duty not to conceal known material defects. The customary vehicle is the **Seller's Property Information Report (SPIR)**, the Vermont REALTORS form, which names "chimney" and "fireplace" in its structural section and asks heating-system type including wood and pellet (form content per Jul 2026 research). **The SPIR is NOT mandated by statute** — Vermont law does not require sellers to complete it; it is used voluntarily by the industry (REF: Peet Law; Bucknam Law). Statutory disclosures that do exist: **flood-risk disclosure, 27 V.S.A. § 380** (added 2024; amended 2025 Acts No. 52, § 2, eff. Sept 1, 2025 — seller provides the FEMA flood insurance rate map or notice of unavailability, whether the property flooded or had flood damage during the seller's ownership, and flood-insurance status; floodready.vermont.gov/disclosure, GOV), groundwater/testing information for homes not on public water, and federal lead-paint disclosure for pre-1978 homes (NATIONAL STANDARD). No inspection is mandated at transfer; NFPA 211 Level 2 stays a NATIONAL STANDARD.

sections.title: Consumer remedies and cancellation rights
sections.markdown: The **Vermont Consumer Protection Act, 9 V.S.A. chapter 63 (§ 2453 prohibits unfair/deceptive acts)**, gives a private right of action and Attorney General enforcement, with damages and attorney's fees (and exemplary damages available). Home-solicitation sales carry a **3-business-day right to cancel under 9 V.S.A. § 2454 ("Purchase contracts; rescission")** — the consumer may cancel until midnight of the third business day; the seller must tender refunds within 10 days. That is the exact mechanic against chimney scare-sales. Complaints: Vermont AG Consumer Assistance Program (run with UVM).

sections.title: Permits and building codes
sections.markdown: **There is no statewide adopted IRC in Vermont.** The **2025 Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code (effective Nov 5, 2025)**, administered by the Division of Fire Safety, adopts **NFPA 1 (2021), NFPA 101 (2021), the 2021 IBC and the 2021 IEBC (structural requirements only)**, with NFPA 70 (2023) and the 2024 International Plumbing Code; it replaced the 2015 Code (in effect Oct 10, 2016 – Nov 5, 2025). The DFS T4 page states NFPA 211 is adopted. **The Code applies only to public buildings (20 V.S.A. ch. 173)**, so owner-occupied single-family homes are outside the state building/fire code; rentals are inside it. A separate statewide Residential Building Energy Standard applies to homes (30 V.S.A. § 51, edition not re-verified). Some municipalities (e.g., Burlington) adopt and enforce local codes. Chimney relines, rebuilds, and solid-fuel appliance installs are permit/code work in public buildings and in municipalities that enforce locally; for a single-family owner-occupied home in a town without local enforcement there may be no permit process.

sections.rawHeading: 6 · CO law (GOV — high confidence; strong at sale)
sections.title: Carbon monoxide and smoke alarm law
sections.markdown: **9 V.S.A. chapter 77** (amended by 2025 Acts No. 69, § 23, eff. July 1, 2025 — current text requires "photoelectric-type or UL 217 compliant" smoke alarms). **§ 2882** requires a builder of a single-family dwelling to install CO alarms in the vicinity of any bedrooms, and requires any single-family dwelling transferred by sale or exchange to contain one or more CO alarms (in dwellings newly constructed after July 1, 2005 with electrical power, CO alarms powered by building electrical service plus battery). "Single-family dwelling" here means a residence not classified as a "public building" or a condominium/multiple-unit dwelling (§ 2881(1)). **§ 2883** — the standout — requires that **at closing of the sale of a single-family dwelling the seller certify to the buyer, signed and dated, that the dwelling is provided with photoelectric-type or UL 217 compliant smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms**; if the buyer notifies the seller by certified mail within 10 days after conveyance that an alarm is not operable, the seller must comply within 10 days; noncompliance does not create a title defect. § 2882 does not require an owner-occupant to maintain the devices afterward. Rentals and other public buildings are covered by the Fire & Building Safety Code (e.g., NFPA 101 § 24.3.4.2 placement). A genuine **pre-sale CO obligation** — a natural tie-in to a chimney/stove inspection at transfer.

sections.title: Solid fuel and environmental rules
sections.markdown: Vermont has among the **highest wood/pellet-heat shares in the nation**, so solid-fuel practice carries the content weight. No statewide burn-ban regime; federal EPA new-stove emission standards apply (NATIONAL STANDARD). Some towns regulate outdoor wood boilers — **name the local ordinance per listing town; VERIFY.**

sections.title: Scam patterns and enforcement
sections.markdown: The Vermont AG's Consumer Assistance Program pursues home-improvement fraud, and the door-knock "we were in the neighborhood / noticed your chimney" pitch is a textbook 9 V.S.A. § 2454 home-solicitation problem. VTDigger (Apr 16, 2026) reported regulators believe many contractors operate unregistered. **Specific VT chimney-sweep enforcement actions: NOT FOUND.** Use pattern language only.

sections.title: Season calendar
sections.markdown: Cold northern-New-England climate; heavy wood heat, long season. Burn season ~Oct–Apr (longer in the Northeast Kingdom/higher elevations). Rush: SEP–NOV. Best booking: APR–JUN.

sections.title: Price seeding (internal)
sections.markdown: Chittenden County (Burlington) and resort towns (Stowe, Manchester) run near/above national; the Northeast Kingdom and rural towns nearer or below national. Regionalize on the Burlington/resort vs rural split.

sections.title: /rights table row (internal)
sections.markdown: License: **YES for sweep work in public buildings (rentals, multi-family, commercial) — DFS T4 Chimney Sweep Certificate of Fitness, requires NCSG-CCP/CCP/CSIA (VFBSC § 1:1.13.1(5)); NOT required for owner-occupied single-family homes; contracting layer is LIGHT registration only (26 V.S.A. ch. 106, > $10k, no exam)** · Registration: **YES — OPR Residential Contractor Registry (> $10k, $1M/$2M insurance); DPS-certified trades EXEMPT (§ 5502(2)(A))** · Disclosure law: **NO general statutory form — SPIR (names chimney/fireplace) is customary, not mandated; statutory flood disclosure (27 V.S.A. § 380)** · 3-day cancel: **YES (9 V.S.A. § 2454)** · CO law: **STRONG — seller certifies compliant CO/smoke alarms at closing of single-family sale (9 V.S.A. §§ 2882–2883)** · Lookup: data.vermont.gov T4 Certifications roster + sos.vermont.gov/residential-contractors + ago.vermont.gov

story.heading: The story
story.markdown: **Vermont is the state that checks the sweep — in the buildings the state already regulates — and checks the alarms at sale.** It is the only state found so far that writes NCSG-CCP/CCP/CSIA certification into a state credential, with a downloadable public roster. But the credential lives inside the Fire & Building Safety Code, which covers public buildings; a homeowner in an owner-occupied single-family house gets no state-required sweep credential, no state building code, and a seller disclosure form that is customary rather than required. What the homeowner does get is unusual: **a seller's written certification of CO alarms at closing.** Page headline: "Vermont certifies sweeps for rentals and public buildings — for your own home, check the roster yourself." The roster being open data makes Vermont the cheapest audit in the country.

faq.q: What should I check before hiring a chimney company in Vermont?
faq.a: State licensing: YES for sweep work in public buildings (rentals, multi-family, commercial) — DFS T4 Chimney Sweep Certificate of Fitness, requires NCSG-CCP/CCP/CSIA (VFBSC § 1:1.13.1(5)); NOT required for owner-occupied single-family homes; contracting layer is LIGHT registration only (26 V.S.A. ch. 106, > $10k, no exam). Registration or credential: YES — OPR Residential Contractor Registry (> $10k, $1M/$2M insurance); DPS-certified trades EXEMPT (§ 5502(2)(A)). Seller disclosure at sale: NO general statutory form — SPIR (names chimney/fireplace) is customary, not mandated; statutory flood disclosure (27 V.S.A. § 380). Right to cancel a sale made at your home: YES (9 V.S.A. § 2454). Carbon monoxide alarm law: STRONG — seller certifies compliant CO/smoke alarms at closing of single-family sale (9 V.S.A. §§ 2882–2883). Where to check a contractor: data.vermont.gov T4 Certifications roster + sos.vermont.gov/residential-contractors + ago.vermont.gov. Then ask the eight questions below, get the inspection findings in writing with photos, and never sign for "emergency" work on the day of a door-knock.
